## Decisions

- ⏳ **open** `b-cjk-line-height` `low confidence` (Matt): Spectrum sets a different line height for Japanese, Korean and Chinese. The contract shape has no language condition, so it is recorded in a note and lost on render. _Evidence: @spectrum-css/badge index.css, .spectrum-Badge-label:lang(ja)_
  - The draft chose: noted on the label part, not expressed
  - If wrong: Add a conditional keyed on language to the contract shape, or accept that generated code omits it.
- ⏳ **open** `b-nonsemantic-colours` `medium confidence` (Matt): Fourteen of the twenty variants are plain colour names with no meaning attached. Do we carry them, or restrict adobe.com to the six semantic ones? _Evidence: index.css, the non-semantic colors comment block_
  - The draft chose: carried all twenty, matching Spectrum
  - If wrong: Narrow the enum if the marketing use only ever needs the semantic set.
- ⏳ **open** `b-host-rules` `high confidence` (Matt): Upstream styles the custom element, so size and the semantic variants are :host([size]) and :host([variant]) rules while the nineteen plain colours are .swc-Badge--<colour> classes. _Evidence: badge.css: :host([variant="accent"]) sets a token; .swc-Badge--blue sets the same token._
  - The draft chose: Re-express both as one variant axis on the root, which is what a light-DOM contract can carry
  - If wrong: If the generated component ever becomes a custom element, drop the re-expression and inherit the host rules.
- ⏳ **open** `b-literal-spacing` `high confidence` (Matt): Badge writes its vertical padding and gap as literals, while Button binds tokens that hold exactly those values. _Evidence: padding 4/7/10/13 is base-padding-vertical-small..extra-large exactly; gap 4/6/6/6 is base-gap-small..extra-large exactly. This is the one place the contract is more token-bound than the implementation._
  - The draft chose: Bind the tokens, matching Button
  - If wrong: Worth raising upstream: if the spacing scale moves, Button follows and Badge does not. If they intend Badge to be independent, revert these six bindings to literals.
- ⏳ **open** `b-design-code-gap` `high confidence` (Matt): The design models this component differently from the implementation, not just with different spelling. _Evidence: The design's Style axis is one choice of three (Bold fill, Subtle fill, Outline); the code has two independent booleans, so subtle and outline can both be set at once, which the design cannot express and which no rule in the stylesheet covers. The design splits the variant across a Status axis and a Color axis; the code has one. The code has a fixed property with four values; the design has none._
  - The draft chose: Map what maps and record the rest
  - If wrong: Raise with the Spectrum team. The style axis in particular is a correctness question, not a naming one.
- ⏳ **open** `b-medium-radius` `high confidence` (Matt): The design file and the implementation disagree about the corner radius at one size. _Evidence: Figma Badge Size=Medium is radius 7 in both the Bold fill and Outline styles; badge.css sets --swc-badge-corner-radius to 8px at :host([size="m"]). Measured at identical settings our badge matches the design on box, fill, padding and gap and differs only here._
  - The draft chose: Follow the implementation, 8px, as the rest of this contract does
  - If wrong: Ask the Spectrum team which is right. The design's sequence across the four sizes is 7, 7, 9, 10, which looks like a skipped step rather than an intent; the implementation's is 7, 8, 9, 10.
- ✅ decided `b-implementation` `high confidence` (Matt): Which package is Spectrum 2's Badge? → The contract describes @adobe/spectrum-wc, the Spectrum 2 web components, for the same reason as Button: the S2 design file's variable names are this package's --swc-* tokens. _Evidence: Badge ships no standalone stylesheet; its CSS is the css`` template in dist/components/badge/badge.js and is vendored unwrapped._
  - The draft chose: @adobe/spectrum-wc (swc-badge)
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `b-modifier-scope` `high confidence` (Matt): Do subtle and outline apply to all twenty-five variants? → Upstream's subtle and outline rules name the six semantic variants and nothing else, so the nineteen plain colours stay solid under either flag. _Evidence: badge.css: :host([subtle][variant="accent"]) and the outline rule list accent, informative, neutral, positive, notice and negative. Applying outline unconditionally turned every colour badge white._
  - The draft chose: No. Both are recorded as combinations with the six semantic variants only.
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `b-fixed-placement` `high confidence` (Matt): What does the fixed property actually change? → fixed sets the two logical corner radii on that edge to zero so the badge sits flush against it. It does not position the badge; placement is the parent's job. _Evidence: badge.css: each .swc-Badge--fixed-* rule sets exactly two border-*-radius values to 0._
  - The draft chose: Squares the two corners on the named edge, nothing else
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `b-label-colour` `high confidence` (Matt): The badge label sat on gray-25, which flips with the theme. → Every badge fill is a saturated or mid colour in both themes, so the label is always white. The subtle and outline treatments are the exception and keep gray-1000, which flips with their tinted fill. _Evidence: Upstream's badge writes a literal rgb(255,255,255) for the label and icon colour. Bound to gray-25 the label rendered near-black on a mid grey fill in dark mode._
  - The draft chose: transparent-static-white-1000, which does not
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `b-warm-label` `high confidence` (Matt): Five fills are too light for a white label. → Both are theme-invariant, because the fills are too. The subtle and outline treatments are the only ones whose label follows the theme, and they keep gray-1000. _Evidence: badge.css gives exactly those five a literal rgb(0, 0, 0) label and icon colour._
  - The draft chose: notice, celery, chartreuse, orange and yellow take a static black label; the other twenty take static white
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `b-radius-gap` `high confidence` (Matt): The four corner radii looked like a token gap, since 7, 8, 9 and 10 are off the corner-radius-100..800 scale. → There is no gap. Spectrum ships a per-size radius family and the badge hardcodes the same numbers instead of referencing it. Our contract binds the tokens. _Evidence: corner-radius-medium-size-{small,medium,large,extra-large} are 7, 8, 9 and 10px; badge.css writes 7px, 8px, 9px and 10px as literals in its four size blocks._
  - The draft chose: Bind corner-radius-medium-size-small through -extra-large, which already hold exactly those four values
  - If wrong: Report upstream: badge.css should reference the corner-radius-medium-size-* family rather than repeat its values.
- ✅ decided `i-glyph-fill` `high confidence` (Matt): Every glyph rendered in its own colour instead of the component's. → Spectrum's workflow SVGs paint with fill="var(--iconPrimary, #222)" rather than currentColor, so with nothing defining that property every glyph fell back to #222 regardless of the colour around it. Setting --iconPrimary to currentColor on the icon part makes a glyph follow its component, and leaves the property available to anyone who wants a different colour. _Evidence: All 396 entries in spectrum-icons.json carry var(--iconPrimary, #222); all 26 in our own s2a-icons.json use currentColor. Measured: the badge's text was #ffffff while its glyph painted #222222._
  - The draft chose: Map the artwork's own hook to currentColor on the part that holds the glyph
  - If wrong: none. The alternative was rewriting 396 vendored SVGs, which would mean editing artwork we do not own.
- ✅ decided `b-subtle-colour-rows` `high confidence` (Matt): The 19 colour variants have subtle backgrounds in shipped code, set in a nested block. Were they missing from the defs? → Yes. The defs were curated on 2026-10-27, before nested rules were read. The 19 rows are added as a fresh draft reads them, in this file's token form. The 6 semantic rows are unchanged. _Evidence: .swc-Badge--subtle{&:where(.swc-Badge--<colour>){--swc-badge-background-color: var(--swc-<colour>-subtle-background-color-default)}} in the css`` template_
  - The draft chose: add the 19 rows
  - If wrong: none

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA: `1.4.3`, `1.4.11`

- Colour alone must not carry the meaning; the label does.
- Spectrum flips the label and icon colour to black on orange, yellow, chartreuse and celery to hold contrast.
